source: FinCEN Advisory on Cyber-Enabled Financial Crime and Account Takeover
section: Advisory FIN-2023-A001: Patterns of Unauthorized Wire Transfers
title: Account Takeover (ATO) with Immediate Total Balance Transfer
content: FinCEN analysis highlights that cybercriminals obtaining unauthorized access to consumer or corporate banking credentials frequently execute a single maximum-balance transfer rather than multiple small increments, in order to bypass periodic aggregate limits before user detection. The hallmark signature is a 100% depletion of the originating account's balance via instantaneous electronic wire.

source: FinCEN Guidance on Funnel Accounts and Money Mule Recruitment
section: Guidance FIN-2022-G004: Identifying Destination Mule Nodes
title: Mule Recipient Profile with Dormant Historical Balances
content: Illicit proceeds are predominantly routed to recipient accounts that show prolonged dormancy or zero balances before suddenly receiving a high-value electronic transfer. In many simulated and real-world core banking attacks, funds are routed to ghost beneficiaries where the core banking ledger records an anomaly in destination balance updates.

source: FinCEN Advisory on Ransomware and Extortion Payment Routing
title: Two-Stage Transfer-and-Cash-Out Exfiltration Sequence
content: Cyber fraud groups utilize a distinct two-step pipeline: (1) An unauthorized TRANSFER from the victim account to an intermediary, immediately followed by (2) a CASH_OUT liquidation transaction. When both transaction types are observed in close proximity with identical amounts, institutions should apply emergency hold protocols.
